title: Timed fallback & tokenized shedding for cross-region dispatch
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: During transient capacity pressure or partial regional outages, our current cross-region dispatch either: (a) immediately failover to next region causing traffic storms and cold-start latency spikes, or (b) over-evict requests locally and degrade SLOs. We need a resilient dispatch algorithm that: 1) prefers low-latency local region while respecting capacity SLOs; 2) progressively and predictably expands failover targets to avoid sudden traffic surges; and 3) performs controlled load shedding when global capacity is constrained.

Proposal: Implement a Timed Fallback and Tokenized Shedding (TFTS) policy as part of the request director. TFTS comprises three coordinated mechanisms:
1) Latency windowed localism: maintain per-population latency histograms and compute a sliding window latency threshold. Only consider remote regions whose tail latency is within an adaptive multiplier of the local window. This keeps affinity tight during normal operation but relaxes when local tails climb.
2) Timed fallbacks: when a region is degraded, we open fallback gates on a staggered timer (t0 -> t1 -> t2). Each gate expands the pool of eligible regions in a controlled cadence (e.g., at 100ms, 300ms, 1s) to avoid surges to any single remote region. Fall back expansion respects per-region admission credits (see tokenized shedding).
3) Tokenized shedding and admission credits: each region exposes a token bucket representing available admission capacity for cross-region acceptance. Director consumes remote tokens when assigning a request to a non-local region. If tokens are exhausted, those remote choices are not eligible. Tokens are refilled based on observed throughput and per-region capacity curves. Token policy prevents cascading overloads and encodes capacity-awareness into routing decisions.

Circuit breakers and SLO mapping: integrate region-level circuit breakers that trip when error-rate or 95th latency exceeds thresholds for a sliding window. Circuit trips immediately remove a region from candidate set; timed fallbacks will re-evaluate it on cool-down. Map product SLOs to routing behavior: higher-tier customers get wider fallback gates and higher admission tokens; free-tier gets stricter pinning and earlier shedding.

Telemetry & observability: emit the following metrics per request: chosen_region, candidate_regions, fallback_gate_level, token_consumed, token_remaining, circuit_state. Expose dashboards for: regional token utilization, fallbacks per minute, cross-region latency delta, shed_count by customer_tier.

Rollout plan: implement feature-flagged controller and director integration; run closed canary against non-critical workloads; A/B compare SLOs (p99 latency and error rates) and token utilization. Gradually widen to production regions with conservative token caps.

Trade-offs considered: tokenized approach avoids all-or-nothing failover but adds complexity and tuning surface (token refill rates, gate timings). Timed gates may add a bit of extra latency for some requests but reduce spike-induced cold starts. We prefer predictable gradual expansion over aggressive hedging because it yields more stable tail behavior and clearer observability.
acceptance_criteria: Director implements TFTS policy behind feature flag and respects per-region token buckets
Unit + e2e tests covering fallback gate progression, token consumption/refill, and circuit trip behavior
Telemetry emitted for gate levels, token metrics, and candidate sets; dashboards created in 'regional-resilience' folder
Canary run in eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 path for 48h with no SLO regressions beyond defined guardrails
Playbook updated with rollback steps and threshold values for token refill and gate timings
comments: 2025-11-11 - Initial design writeup posted to Confluence; requested review from SRE and Platform teams. (see links)
2025-11-13 - SRE feedback: prefer token refill paced by short-term EWMA of accepted throughput rather than fixed timers to adapt to burstier traffic. Added to design notes.

2025-11-17 - Platform review: prefer gate timings expressed as percentiles (e.g., open next gate when 95th exceeds X) in addition to absolute timers. Decided to implement both: timers for predictability + percentile triggers for sensitivity.

2025-11-19 - Prototype in testbed: tokenized shedding reduced remote admission spikes by ~42% in synthetic overload run. Observed slight p99 increase (~60ms) for cross-region accepted requests. Captured results in PR comments.

2025-11-21 - Design review w/ PM: tiered token caps approved (Enterprise=3x, Standard=1x, Free=0.5x). PM requested explicit customer-facing degradation messaging for free-tier; added to acceptance criteria.

2025-11-24 - Implementation in progress: director hooks added, token bucket library landed in runtime-utils (PR #1284). Next: integrate refill strategy and dashboard panels. Assigned to Marco for rollout coordination.
